description: SPSC producer/consumer pipeline (StagedProcessor) vs single-threaded direct InstrumentRegistry replay -- throughput and enqueue-to-complete latency, steady_limit_flow scenario, OptimizedMatcher backend on both sides.
method: benchmarks/bench_pipeline.cpp: loads steady_limit_flow (20000 ops, symbolCount=1, single symbol "SYM0"). runDirect() replays ops on the calling thread against InstrumentRegistry directly, timestamping each op individually. runPipeline() spawns a producer thread that calls StagedProcessor::enqueue*() for each op (sequence-numbered) while StagedProcessor's own consumer thread drains a 4095-usable-slot SpscQueue<PipelineEvent> and applies each event to its own InstrumentRegistry instance; latency is enqueueTimeNs (stamped by the producer, before any full-queue spin) to apply-time, recorded by the consumer's callback. Ran 5 times back-to-back in one process; numbers vary run to run (no repeated-trial averaging like bench_match's Google Benchmark harness) -- both the range and the last (warmest) run are reported below.

throughput_ops_per_sec.note: Pipeline throughput is comparable to (not reliably faster or slower than) direct replay -- expected, since the consumer does the identical InstrumentRegistry work as the direct path, plus queue transit.

root_cause_of_pipeline_latency.finding: Pipeline per-event latency is ~1.3-2.1ms across all 5 runs, roughly 4 orders of magnitude above direct per-op latency, and p50/p99/p999 sit close together (a plateau, not a long tail).
root_cause_of_pipeline_latency.explanation: This synthetic benchmark's producer has no real per-op cost of its own (unlike a real ITCH feed, which is naturally rate-limited by decode + I/O) -- it can enqueue faster than the consumer, doing the same InstrumentRegistry work as the direct path, can drain. The queue (kPipelineQueueCapacity=4096, usable capacity 4095) saturates almost immediately and stays saturated for the whole run, so nearly every event queues behind a near-full buffer. Steady-state queueing delay for a saturated bounded queue is approximately capacity / consumer_throughput; at the observed ~3M ops/sec consumer rate that's ~4095/3e6s = ~1.36ms, which matches the measured plateau. This was verified with a standalone instrumented run (not checked in) that logged per-event latency growing linearly from ~80us to ~1.08ms as the queue filled, then plateauing -- confirming genuine backpressure, not a scheduling bug. Removing the producer's/consumer's std::this_thread::yield() spin-wait (tested, then reverted) made no measurable difference, ruling out yield()-related scheduling artifacts as the cause.
root_cause_of_pipeline_latency.implication: This SPSC pipeline does not reduce per-op latency over direct replay, and this benchmark cannot show the scenario where it would: a real feed's producer thread is bottlenecked on network/decode I/O, leaving the consumer's queue mostly empty so it can absorb bursts without building a backlog. The measured number is reported as-is -- no latency win is implied here.

macos_caveat: StagedProcessor::pinThread() is a no-op on macOS (sched_setaffinity/pthread_setaffinity_np have no macOS equivalent for pinning arbitrary threads to specific cores) -- both producer and consumer are scheduled entirely by the OS, unlike a pinned Linux deployment. This is unrelated to the queueing-driven latency above (confirmed via the instrumented standalone run), but is disclosed for completeness.

correctness.note: StressNoLostOrDuplicateEvents replays 100,000 sequence-numbered events through StagedProcessor and asserts appliedSequences() is exactly [0..99999] with no gaps or repeats -- the SPSC FIFO guarantee holds under real cross-thread contention, not just in principle. MatchesDirectReplayOnBookAndTradeCount confirms bestBid/bestAsk-equivalent (bidDepth/askDepth(10)) and total trade count are identical between the pipeline and a direct single-threaded replay of the same 5000-op sequence.

notes: ReferenceMatcher, matching/crossing semantics, and ItchEngineAdapter message handling were not modified for this pipeline.
The single-threaded replay path (EventReplayer, replay_engine) is untouched and still builds/runs as before.
The pipeline's value here is correctness under concurrency (determinism, no lost/duplicate events, clean shutdown), not a measured latency or throughput win.
